qa.name: Extensor Hallucis Brevis
qa.origin: Anterior and lateral surfaces of the calcaneus (superolateral surface); inferior extensor retinaculum
qa.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe
qa.innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L5, S1); extends great toe
qa.function: Extends the metatarsophalangeal joint of the great toe
qa.opposing_muscle: Flexor Hallucis Longus and Brevis (great toe flexion)
qa.blood_supply: Dorsalis pedis artery; lateral tarsal artery
qa.clinical_note: Extensor Hallucis Brevis is the medial part of the muscle belly that arises from the calcaneus — it is often described as a separate muscle from Extensor Digitorum Brevis but they share the same origin. A soft swelling over the lateral dorsum of the foot at the sinus tarsi is often mistaken for a ganglion but may represent hypertrophy of the EDB/EHB muscle belly — a common incidental finding. Both dorsal foot muscles are innervated by the deep fibular nerve (L5–S1), the same nerve that supplies the anterior compartment of the leg.

qa.name: Extensor Digitorum Brevis
qa.origin: Anterior and lateral surfaces of the calcaneus; inferior extensor retinaculum
qa.insertion: Lateral sides of the tendons of Extensor Digitorum Longus to toes 2–4
qa.innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L5, S1); extends toes 2–4
qa.function: Extends the metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints of toes 2–4
qa.opposing_muscle: Flexor Digitorum Longus and Brevis (toe flexion)
qa.blood_supply: Dorsalis pedis artery; lateral tarsal artery
qa.clinical_note: Extensor Digitorum Brevis is the only intrinsic muscle on the dorsum of the foot — all other intrinsic foot muscles are plantar. Its fleshy belly is visible on the lateral dorsum of the foot and can be palpated during active toe extension. It assists EDL in extending toes 2–4. The deep fibular nerve terminates on the dorsum of the foot supplying EDB and EHB — its sensory distribution is the first web space between the great and second toes. Loss of sensation here with preserved toe extension suggests a lesion distal to where the nerve supplies EDB.
